title: Enhancing students’ authentic mathematical problem-solving skills and confidence through error analysis of GPT-4 solutions
venue: Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning
extended_summary:
This study asks whether an error-analysis learning activity built around GPT-4-generated mathematical solutions can improve elementary students’ ability to solve authentic, real-life mathematics problems and increase their mathematical confidence. The authors focus on the challenge that authentic word problems are cognitively demanding for students, especially lower-achieving learners, and explore whether AI output can be transformed from a potential source of incorrect answers into a productive learning resource.

The intervention was a ten-week quasi-experimental classroom study with 59 fifth-grade students in a primary school in northern Taiwan. The experimental group worked in small heterogeneous groups to analyze GPT-4 solutions to authentic mathematics problems, mark errors, discuss corrections with peers, and present their reasoning to the class, while the control group received traditional instruction using the same materials. Outcomes were measured with pre/post authentic mathematical problem-solving tests, a TIMSS-based mathematical confidence scale, and semi-structured interviews with the experimental group.

Results showed that the experimental group improved significantly from pre- to post-test in authentic mathematical problem-solving and mathematical confidence. Between-group comparisons favored the experimental group, with statistically significant advantages for low-achieving students on problem-solving and for both high- and low-achieving students on confidence. Interview data suggested that GPT-4 explanations supported understanding, peer discussion, critical thinking, and metacognitive reflection. The authors conclude that GPT-4, when paired with structured error analysis and collaboration, can be an effective instructional support in elementary mathematics, particularly for helping lower-achieving students.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental study with a comparison group, but it is not randomized and uses purposive sampling from one school. The mixed quantitative/qualitative design supports credible inference, though selection bias and limited generalizability remain concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention produced statistically significant improvements in mathematical confidence and within-group gains in authentic math problem solving, with a notable subgroup benefit for low-achieving students. However, effect sizes are not reported, and the between-group overall achievement difference was only marginal, so the impact appears modest rather than large.

interventions.use_case: GPT-4-generated worked solutions used by fifth-grade students for authentic mathematics problem solving, followed by error analysis of the AI’s solution steps in small-group discussion and class presentation

finding.finding_summary: The experimental group improved significantly on authentic mathematical problem-solving after 10 weeks of GPT-4 error-analysis activities (within-group Wilcoxon z=-4.318, p<.001; n=28). Between groups, post-test performance was higher for the experimental group overall, and the low-achieving subgroup showed a significant advantage over controls (U=48, p=.01), indicating stronger benefits for lower performers.
finding.measure: Authentic Mathematical Problem-Solving Test (AMPS) pre/post scores

finding.finding_summary: Mathematical confidence increased significantly in the experimental group after the intervention (within-group Wilcoxon z=-3.881, p<.001; n=28). Post-test confidence was also significantly higher than control overall (U=215, p=.001), with significant gains for both high-achieving (U=64, p=.045) and low-achieving students (U=43, p=.007).
finding.measure: TIMSS 2019 Mathematical Confidence Scale (9-item Likert scale)

finding.finding_summary: Interview data indicated improvements in understanding, collaborative problem-solving, critical thinking, mathematical creativity, and metacognitive knowledge after students worked with GPT-4 solutions and analyzed errors. The authors report that 93% of experimental-group students said GPT-4 improved understanding, 79% reported better collaboration, and 86% reported gains in metacognitive knowledge, but no standardized effect sizes were provided.
finding.measure: Semi-structured interview themes and coded response proportions
